{"filepath":"executive_briefing.md","content":"Executive Briefing: Grid-Scale Storage — Cost vs Duration
Date: 06 Sep 2026

Purpose and scope
-----------------
This briefing summarizes a focused comparison of grid-scale energy storage technologies to inform near-term procurement and pilot decisions. It builds on the analysis delivered by the team (cost_duration_analysis.csv) and synthesizes the key quantitative trade-offs between energy CAPEX, usable duration, round‑trip efficiency and levelized cost of capacity (LCOC). The intent is operational: give executives a concise recommendation for short (<4 h), medium (4–12 h) and long (>12 h) duration needs, and a single prioritized action to start immediately.

Methods (high level)
---------------------
- Source: cost_duration_analysis.csv (Bob). Median values and sensitivity ranges in that file were used.
- LCOC and CAPEX figures reflect the authors' stated assumptions (baseline: real discount rate ≈7%, representative lifetimes and cycles/year); see the CSV for the full assumptions and sensitivity bounds.
- This memo does not repeat the CSV detail; it translates the key outputs into an actionable recommendation and next steps.

Key quantitative comparison (selected metrics)
---------------------------------------------
Data source: cost_duration_analysis.csv (Bob). Table below pulls the principal median metrics from the provided analysis.

| Technology | Median CAPEX (USD/kWh) | Median duration (hours) | Median efficiency (%) | Median LCOC (USD/kWh) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lithium-ion (Li-ion) | 182.50 | 3.50 | 90 | 0.0808 |
| Supercapacitors | 3,000.00 | 0.1505 | 90 | 0.0130 |

Notes: the CSV includes additional technologies and sensitivity ranges; the four columns above are the most decision-relevant summary metrics. LCOC in the CSV is computed using the stated CRF / life / cycles assumptions — LCOC is sensitive to assumed cycles/yr, lifespan and installed system BOS costs.

Recommendation (short, medium, long + single prioritized action)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Short-duration (<4 h)
- Primary: Lithium-ion batteries. Rationale: best commercial maturity and project-readiness for 1–4 h firming and ancillary services; competitive median LCOC for frequent cycling. Supercapacitors/flywheels are best for ultra-short (<~0.25 h) high-power applications (frequency regulation, sub-second response) but do not substitute for 1–4 h energy.

Medium-duration (4–12 h)
- Primary: Flow batteries (vanadium/iron) or other long-duration chemistries. Rationale: technology design targets (independent energy vs power capacity) and stable performance for multi-hour discharge. The cost_duration_analysis.csv shows Li-ion median duration ≈3.5 h — short of the 4–12 h band — so an alternative chemistry is recommended for medium-duration requirements.

Long-duration (>12 h)
- Primary: Bulk/seasonal options (pumped hydro, compressed air, thermal storage where site-appropriate). Rationale: these technologies offer materially lower cost per stored MWh for long-duration needs once site constraints and permitting are satisfied.

Single prioritized recommendation for immediate action
- Issue a targeted RFP and fund a pilot procurement for a 4-hour-capable Li-ion system (example pilot size: 10 MW / 40 MWh) and concurrently initiate a short feasibility study on flow-battery options for 4–12 h needs.
  - Why this first: Li-ion is commercially de-risked and can be delivered quickly to realize short-term network benefits and revenue streams; the 4-h capability is rapidly becoming the market standard for peak-shifting and capacity services. Running both a Li-ion pilot and a flow-battery feasibility keeps options open for medium-duration requirements.

Rationale (concise)
--------------------
- Speed to value: Li-ion vendors and EPCs are mature; procurement-to-commissioning timelines are shorter than for flow batteries or bulk storage.
- Cost-competitiveness: Li-ion median LCOC (≈$0.0808/kWh) is attractive for frequent cycling use cases. Supercapacitors show very low LCOC at ultra-short durations but are not energy solutions for hour-scale needs.
- Portfolio fit: A two-track approach (deploy Li-ion for short-duration and pilot flow or bulk for multi-hour/seasonal needs) balances near-term wins with strategic long-duration ambition.

Key risks & uncertainties
-------------------------
- CAPEX variance: the CSV shows wide capex ranges (±50% or more) across technologies — project-specific procurement prices can materially change LCOC.
- Lifetime & cycles assumptions: LCOC is highly sensitive to assumed cycles/year and lifetime (calendar and cycle degradation); real-world operational profiles can diverge from model assumptions.
- Supply chain & lead times: Li-ion cells remain sensitive to raw material supply and cyclical price swings; long‑duration chemistries may face vendor concentration and longer lead times.
- Safety / permitting: Li-ion systems carry fire-safety and permitting considerations that require site-specific mitigation and may extend schedules.
- Revenue uncertainty: market/regulatory changes (capacity market design, ancillary service prices) will affect project economics.

Three recommended next steps (actionable, with rough cost/time)
---------------------------------------------------------------
1) Issue an RFP and authorize a Li-ion 4-hour pilot (10 MW / 40 MWh example)
   - Scope: procurement, BOS, integration, commissioning, 12-month performance trial with commercial-operation targets.
   - Rough cost (capex-focused): energy CAPEX ≈ $182.5/kWh × 40,000 kWh ≈ $7.3M (energy modules only); installed system + BOS + contingency ≈ $8–12M. (Source: cost_duration_analysis.csv median CAPEX.)
   - Timeline: procurement → 9–12 months to commercial operation (site permitting and interconnection permitting timelines can extend this).
   - Owner: Procurement/Generation lead + legal/commercial.

2) Run a focused flow-battery feasibility and vendor down‑select (4–12 h target)
   - Scope: technical-feasibility (site, water use, footprint), vendor quotations, lifecycle LCOC modelling with project-specific cycles, and risk assessment.
   - Rough cost: $100–250k for procurement of studies and vendor RFQ responses.
   - Timeline: 8–12 weeks to decision-ready report.
   - Owner: Strategy / Storage program manager.

3) Update financial model & sensitivity analysis and finalize commercial decision framework
   - Scope: produce a project-level financial model (CAPEX/OPEX/LCOC/revenue stacks) for shortlisted options (Li-ion pilot, flow-battery, bulk-storage), including downside scenarios and safety/regulatory cost adders.
   - Rough cost: $50–100k (internal PM + specialist modelling / consulting time).
   - Timeline: 4–6 weeks after vendor quotes and pilot budget clarity.
   - Deliverable: Go/no-go recommendation for scale deployment and procurement strategy.

Appendix
--------
- Primary dataset: cost_duration_analysis.csv (Bob). That file contains the full technology list, assumptions and sensitivity runs used to generate the median and range figures cited above.
- Supporting market research and vendor notes: market_research.csv (available in the project folder) — review recommended before issuing RFPs.

Bottom line
-----------
For near-term, high-confidence wins: prioritize Li-ion 4‑hour systems (pilot RFP now). Simultaneously invest in a short feasibility track for flow batteries to cover medium-duration needs; pursue bulk/seasonal options only where site and permitting support them. The two-track plan balances speed, cost certainty, and a path to lower-cost multi‑hour storage.

Prepared by: Strategy / Storage Analysis Team
(Data source: cost_duration_analysis.csv — Bob)"}
